content.user_title: Protect Environment Secrets in AI Sessions
content.value_statement: Secrets can leak through AI chats, terminal output, logs, and commits. This skill provides concise practices for handling environment variables safely with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use secure environment variable handling during AI-assisted development.
Provides guidance for keeping secrets out of Claude sessions.
Highlights terminal, log, and git commit exposure risks for environment variables.
Frames the skill as prompt-only guidance, with no scripts or automated scanning.
Links to a source repository for users who need more information.
limitations: It does not include executable scripts or automated secret detection.
It cannot verify that a repository is free of leaked credentials.
It depends on the user applying the guidance consistently.
The source file provides high-level guidance, not detailed platform-specific procedures.

use_cases.title: Review AI Session Safety
use_cases.description: Review secret-handling habits before asking an AI agent to inspect or modify configuration files.

use_cases.title: Define Environment Variable Rules

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Secret Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the varlock guidance to review my plan for storing project secrets. Identify places where credentials could enter chat, logs, terminals, or commits.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants a simple safety review before sharing environment details.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Safe AI Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pre-session checklist for using Claude Code with private environment variables. Include what to hide, redact, and avoid pasting.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants safer setup before asking an agent to work on a project.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Configuration Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this environment variable workflow for leak paths across shell history, logs, CI output, and git commits. Recommend safer handling steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team wants to find exposure points in an existing workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Design Team Guardrails
prompt_templates.prompt: Design team guidance for using Claude, Codex, and Claude Code with sensitive environment variables. Include review checkpoints, redaction rules, and escalation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: A security lead wants reusable standards for AI-assisted development.

output_examples.input: Review my plan to paste a production token into a prompt so the model can debug an API issue.
output: Do not paste the token into the session.
Use a redacted placeholder and describe the token purpose.
Share the error text only after removing credentials and account identifiers.

output_examples.input: Create a checklist for safe AI work on a project with environment variables.
output: Confirm no real secrets appear in prompts, screenshots, logs, or terminal output.
Use placeholder names for sensitive values.
Review pending commits for environment files and unredacted logs.

output_examples.input: Help define team rules for using Claude Code with private settings.
output: Keep real credentials outside the AI session.
Describe configuration intent instead of sharing secret values.
Escalate any suspected exposure before continuing work.

best_practices: Redact secrets before sharing prompts, screenshots, terminal output, or logs.
Use placeholders and describe variable purpose instead of exposing real values.
Review git diffs and commit history for accidental credential exposure.
anti_patterns: Pasting real API keys or tokens into an AI session.
Asking an agent to print all environment variables for troubleshooting.
Committing environment files or unredacted logs to a repository.

faq.question: Does this skill manage secrets automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance only and does not run tools, scan files, or change settings.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance applies to Codex, Claude, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it replace a secrets manager?
faq.answer: No. Use a dedicated secrets manager for storage, rotation, and access control.

faq.question: What should I share instead of real secret values?
faq.answer: Share placeholders, variable names, expected formats, and sanitized error messages.

faq.question: Can it prove my repository has no leaked credentials?
faq.answer: No. Use secret scanning tools and manual review for that assurance.

faq.question: Why does the report mention network findings?
faq.answer: The scanner detected source repository URLs. They are documentation links, not runtime network calls.
